Perimeter Institute's own PSI programme landing page. Authoritative for what the programme is and what degree is awarded.

awarding_body.detail: The pages read are on perimeterinstitute.ca, Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics' own domain, not a mirror or aggregator. Perimeter is the awarding body for the scholarship and for the PSI certificate. One nuance: the master's degree itself is conferred by the University of Waterloo, with which PSI runs 'in collaboration'.
awarding_body.quote: students at PSI are fully integrated into the unique international culture and dynamic research atmosphere at Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics ... while earning a Master of Science from the University of Waterloo in Ontario, Canada. ... Successful graduates will earn a Master of Science in Physics degree from the University of Waterloo, as well as a Perimeter Scholars International certificate from Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics.

deadline.detail: The How to Apply page states 'Applications are now open' with a deadline of Sunday January 24, 2027 at 11:59 pm ET, matching the record's 'January 24, 2027, 11:59 pm ET' / 2027-01-24 exactly. The application portal independently gives 'Appl Deadline: 2027/01/24 23:59:59' for the 2027 PSI intake. This is a currently-open cycle. Two caveats for the reviewer: (1) the FAQ page still shows the previous cycle's date, 'February 1, 2026 at 11:59pm EST', which is stale; (2) the deadline is stated as a 'first consideration' date rather than an absolute cut-off, since late applications may be considered until positions are filled.
deadline.quote: Deadline for submission is Sunday January 24, 2027 at 11:59 pm ET

eligibility.detail: Both eligibility claims confirmed. The page requires an undergraduate degree in physics and/or math, matching the record's 'physics, mathematics ... or a related field'. The 'exceptional cases' route and its five required topics are word-for-word identical to the record. The record's 'strong academic record' is supported by 'exceptional, enthusiastic and engaging students'. One claim I could not confirm and which is in fact contradicted: the record describes the programme as 'Open to applicants from outside Canada', but no such restriction appears. Perimeter admits 'students from countries around the world' and the financial-support page explicitly addresses 'Canadian PSI applicants', and a Canadian student testimonial is published, so Canadian nationals are eligible too.
eligibility.quote: Perimeter Scholars International master's program welcomes and encourages exceptional, enthusiastic and engaging students with an undergraduate degree in physics and/or math. ... In exceptional cases, students with other degrees may be considered, provided they can demonstrate understanding of relevant undergraduate-level topics in: Classical mechanics, Electromagnetism, Special relativity, Quantum mechanics, Statistical physics

funding.detail: 'Fully Funded' is accurate. The page lists a full scholarship covering tuition, accommodation, meals, a living stipend, health insurance, IT equipment and learning materials, and a travel supplement. It is not tuition-only. Two qualifications worth recording: coverage is extended 'to up to all accepted students' rather than to every accepted student, and the provisions 'have no cash value and are provided as-is'.
funding.quote: Full scholarships are available to cover: - Full tuition - Accommodation - Meals - Living stipend - Health insurance - Necessary IT equipment and learning materials - Travel supplement

degree_levels.detail: Master's only, as the record says. PSI is a one-year, condensed master's programme (the FAQ says 'The program will run for typically ten months'). A separate two-year PSI pilot exists but is selected from students already enrolled in the one-year programme, so it is not an independent entry-level award.
degree_levels.quote: PSI is a condensed one-year program offered in collaboration with the University of Waterloo.

recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Re-checked live 2026-10-12 against perimeterinstitute.ca. All checks pass; the FAQ page at /training/masters-program/psi-frequently-asked-questions still carries a stale previous-cycle deadline ('February 1, 2026 at 11:59pm EST') and should be corrected by the awarding body or ignored. The How to Apply page (/training/masters-program/psi-how-apply) is the better source for eligibility and exact deadline wording than the financial-support page currently recorded. The deadline is a 'first consideration' date - late applications may be considered until all positions are filled. Deadlines for this programme recur on the same late-January date each year, so the next re-check should confirm the 2028 cycle date around autumn 2027. Also flag the eligibility wording: the programme is open to applicants worldwide including Canadians, so the record's 'from outside Canada' framing is an over-restriction.

notes_for_reviewer: Four things a human should weigh. (1) The record's eligibility text says 'Open to applicants from outside Canada'. Perimeter's own pages do not support that restriction: they admit 'students from countries around the world', the financial-support page addresses 'Canadian PSI applicants', and a Canadian alumnus is quoted. I would suggest rewording to 'open to applicants worldwide, including Canada' rather than 'from outside Canada'. (2) 'Fully Funded' is correct, but note 'Scholarships are extended to up to all accepted students' - it is a full scholarship, not an unconditional guarantee for every admitted student. (3) Perimeter's own FAQ page contradicts its own How to Apply page on the deadline (Feb 1, 2026 vs Jan 24, 2027); I treated the How to Apply page and the AcademicJobsOnline listing as authoritative because the FAQ date is in the past and the current cycle is the 2027 PSI intake. (4) The Master of Science is granted by the University of Waterloo; Perimeter grants the certificate and the scholarship. The record's awarding_body is correct for the scholarship, but applicants should know the degree-granting institution is Waterloo.
